evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Colonies, relocation and losses
evidence.text: Removing your last ship from a planet immediately loses that colony. Returning ships must go to **existing** colonies, not abandoned planets; if no colony can receive a required relocation, those ships go to warp unless an explicit exception applies. You still defend an empty home planet with zero ships. Extra ship losses normally let the losing player choose their ships, unless the effect specifies someone else. A requirement to lose ships outside the encounter cannot be paid with encounter ships; if you have no eligible ships, lose none. Likewise you cannot activate a sacrifice requiring an outside ship by substituting an inside ship. Forced losses/sacrifices normally choose ships you control, not ships already in warp, removed or captured.

evidence.heading: Turn Structure / 3. Launch
evidence.text: The offense chooses one planet in the destiny-indicated system and aims the gate at it. Place one to four offense ships on the **wide end of the hyperspace gate**, drawn from any combination of the offense's existing home and foreign colonies. You may strip a colony, but removing its last ship immediately eliminates it. Ships returning from an encounter or warp cannot return to that now-empty location as though it remained your colony.

The FAQ adds that a player who has no colonies or ships on their turn may instead place the Regroup ship on any home planet. Ordinary relocation with no colony to receive ships sends them to the warp; the stated Regroup exceptions take precedence.

evidence.heading: 2. Destiny
evidence.quote:
### 2. Destiny

Draw destiny to determine the defense and target system. **When only one card remains, do not draw it**: shuffle it with the destiny discards, then draw from the new deck.

- Another player's color: encounter that player in their home system.
- Your own color: redraw, or target one chosen foreign colony in your home system, making its owner the defense. Other colonies there are bystanders. You can instead aim at a home planet with **no ships of any color**, moving up to four ships from other colonies there to reclaim it automatically. This counts as a win and successful encounter, proceeds only through Launch, and can qualify you for a second encounter.
- Wild: choose another player and encounter them in their home system.
- Special: follow its conditions, defense and location. The original rulebook's illustrated special card chooses the other player with the most current foreign colonies, excluding offense. Break a tie toward offense's left, choosing the first tied eligible player there; encounter that player in their home system (rulebook p7). For color-dependent effects such as Shadow, treat it as the designated defense's color.

Destiny hazard symbols have no effect in this base game. Ordinarily you cannot attack a player's foreign colony in a third player's system: a color/wild/special targets its defense in that player's home system, while your own color permits driving out a foreign colony in your own system. If you already have colonies on **all planets in the defensive system**, draw destiny again.

evidence.heading: Actions / Morph
evidence.text: The single base Morph becomes an exact copy of the opponent's initially revealed encounter card: attack copies its initial value, negotiate becomes negotiate. Resolve that pairing normally. Subsequent modifications of the opponent's card do not automatically carry over to Morph; Morph can be modified separately. For example, Tripler revealing Morph against attack12 copies12 and divides its own copy to4; Tripler revealing12 against Morph changes its own12 to4, while opponent's Morph remains12. After resolution, Morph returns to its normal identity and is normally discarded with the other revealed encounter card, unless an effect changes its destination. If two Morphs could be played against each other, both sides would lose all involved ships to warp; there is only one in this base deck.

evidence.heading: Actions / Attack against negotiate: compensation
evidence.text: The negotiate player automatically loses; resolve the winner's ship destinations normally. The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

The losing main player randomly takes one card from the opponent's hand for each of **their own ships actually lost to the warp**. Exclude allied losses: allies receive no compensation. If the opponent lacks sufficient cards, take the entire hand. Cards are taken without seeing their faces. Compensation is stolen hand cards; defender rewards are deck draws and/or warp retrieval.

evidence.heading: Actions / Attack against attack
evidence.text:
- **Offense wins:** all offense and offensive ally ships land on the target, establishing or reinforcing each color's colony. Defense and defensive ally ships go to warp. Bystanders survive. Advance a colony marker only for a newly established foreign colony, not reinforcement of an existing colony.
- **Defense wins:** defending and bystander colonies stay. Offense and offensive allies go to warp. Defensive allies return their committed ships to any existing own colonies, even different origins; helping defend does not grant a colony on the defended planet. Each defensive ally must collect **one defender reward per ship contributed**. For each contributed ship, draw one cosmic-deck card or retrieve one own warp ship to any own colony; combine these choices freely. The ordinary rule does not permit declining these rewards. Declare the full mix of card draws and warp-ship retrievals **before taking any rewards**; do not inspect an initial draw before deciding the remaining sources (official FAQ p8's base-relevant reward-source rule).

evidence.heading: Special Rules & Edge Cases / Colonies, relocation and losses
evidence.text: Removing your last ship from a planet immediately loses that colony. Returning ships must go to **existing** colonies, not abandoned planets; if no colony can receive a required relocation, those ships go to warp unless an explicit exception applies. You still defend an empty home planet with zero ships. Extra ship losses normally let the losing player choose their ships, unless the effect specifies someone else. A requirement to lose ships outside the encounter cannot be paid with encounter ships; if you have no eligible ships, lose none. Likewise you cannot activate a sacrifice requiring an outside ship by substituting an inside ship. Forced losses/sacrifices normally choose ships you control, not ships already in warp, removed or captured.

evidence.text: **FAQ pp3,15:** Compensation versus defender rewards follows normal offense/defense/other-player timing. The selected target cannot interrupt your hand-targeting effect by dumping reinforcements after their Reveal window has passed.

evidence.heading: Start Turn and hand replacement
evidence.quote:
### Start Turn and hand replacement

Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of your turn, before Regroup effects. If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards. You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them. Hate draws a needed starting hand before using its power.

At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.

Carry out the relevant outcome, compensation and other effects. Discard revealed encounter cards after resolving the encounter, unless an effect changes their destination. Check ordinary victory at the very end of Resolution. Then have an eligible optional second encounter or pass left.
